answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can be achieved by requiring each identity to maintain an active jetty of outbound verification probes into a shared ocean of peer task results. To unlock privileges, the agent assembles a unique wharf of timestamped, challengeable interaction logs that peers randomly audit. Attackers incur the cost of continuously operating distinct, non-reusable probe sequences for every fake identity, because recycled logs fail cryptographic freshness checks and consume real network and compute resources without building transferable standing.
